title: Sepsis, severe sepsis, septic shock, urosepsis and bacteremia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the sepsis, severe sepsis or septic shock only (not the local infection or the organ dysfunction). If none applies, choose 'no code'.
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026

Reason for Admission: Sepsis and skin infection.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Positive for fever, chills, and malaise.
Integumentary: Positive for localized erythema and warmth of the right lower extremity.
Respiratory: Negative for shortness of breath or cough.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain or palpitations.
Neurological: Negative for confusion or dizziness.

HPI (Copied Forward): Patient is a 77-year-old woman who presented with a painful, red area on her right leg. She reports a low-grade fever and feeling generally unwell. She denies any recent travel or known exposure to infectious diseases.

Hospital Course: The patient was admitted for sepsis resulting from a skin infection. Cultures identified the pathogen as methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA). She was started on intravenous cefazolin for infection management. She remained stable throughout her stay and showed rapid improvement in clinical markers. She was transitioned to oral medications prior to discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
- Sepsis
- Skin infection due to methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA)

Discharge Medications:
- Cefazolin 750mg every 8 hours (finish 7-day course)
- Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours as needed for fever/pain

Follow-up: Return to primary care physician in 7 days for wound check and medication review.

Electronically signed,
R. Mensah, MD
05/15/2026
explanations: Sepsis due to methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus: A41.01 (HCC 2).
